questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code applies backpressure to incoming booking requests? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The slot service becomes very slow. What limits how many reservations are in flight at once?
choices: The 512-element queue buffer, which holds in-flight reservations
The throttle of 50 elements per second, which also bounds concurrent calls
The `mapAsync(reserveParallelism)` stage, which allows at most 8 outstanding reserve calls
Nothing: each submitted request starts its own reserve call immediately

questions.prompt: A call to `slots.reserve` fails with an exception for one request while others are healthy. What happens to the stream and to that request?
choices: The stream fails and is torn down, so the queue stops accepting offers
The request is handed to `ParkedRequests` and the stream keeps processing later requests
The request is retried automatically with the same parallelism until it succeeds
The request is silently skipped and only logged as a warning

questions.prompt: Which statement about the notification stage is correct?
choices: It can send at most about 50 confirmations per second sustained, and when it falls behind it stops demanding from the reserve stage
It sends confirmations in parallel with unlimited concurrency since the throttle only delays the first element
It sends confirmations out of order because mapAsync(2) emits results as they complete
It drops confirmations above 50 per second to protect the notifier
